objective: Under the owner's standing mandate to run research on our own, SPHERE-GROWTH-20261107-001's next step (grow K_m by a local process, Payoff 2/3, Concreteness 2/3), sharpened: does a growing law need the hidden bit at all? A finished sphere cannot be checked as round without a hidden bit per incidence. Compare growth by refinement (subdividing every triangle) with growth by accretion (adding triangles at the boundary, ring by ring around a corner), with results that hold in every growth order: which needs a witness, and why? Serves question 9 (a law that grows its own space, nothing drawn).
status: Complete 2026-11-07: growth keeps a knot sphere round without a witness only by refinement, which scales a round seed and never places a corner; accretion must place corners, and with turns decided by a label-free local rule it also closes lopsided spheres (38 distinct closures up to 100 triangles, 3 round; 12 of 400 random-coin runs non-round), so making the four equator corners agree needs a carried bit, a hidden witness. Recommendation: Continue with hardness without roundness (G3), Payoff 2/3 Substantial, Concreteness 2/3 Testable.
stop_rule: Stop when refinement and accretion are each answered (memory needed or not, how much), by proof or computation, or an obstruction is found and explained.
title: A growing law needs a shared coin: refinement shares it, accretion must carry it
